catalog.title: Fit a J-lens
catalog.mac: Research methods: Author request, review inputs, then open execution and evidence. Both CLIs use science interview/draft/publish and the same managed engine.
outputs: Immutable fitting run, float32 Jacobians, fitting report, checkpoint, and a ready-to-import artifact description.
catalog.restriction: Fits with the pinned reference Jacobian estimator on a prepared, unquantized checkpoint. Start with a small timing pilot. Automatic scheduler resume is disabled; an explicit checkpoint continues in a new reviewed run. Export/fetch/import returns completed runs; artifact-plan/import then registers the lens. Partial checkpoint recovery uses permitted file transfer. Fitting is not qualification or behavioral evidence.

actions.authorityReason: Inspect staged scientific inputs and execution resources without execution or authorship.
Execute a reviewed scientific operation and retain its scientific output type.

access.restriction: Calls the existing route with its existing service role and scientific gates. Request path parameters, query and body remain explicit; this adapter does not change execution topology or retry mutations.

interview.title: Fit a new J-lens
interview.purpose: Build a model-specific instrument that maps intermediate residual activations into the final-layer basis. Choose your text, measure a pilot, and retain the fitting recipe.

fields.label: Model to fit
fields.help: Choose a prepared Hugging Face checkpoint. Fitting does not download model weights or change them.

fields.label: Exact model version
fields.help: Inspect the model to pin its 40-character commit. The resulting lens belongs to this checkpoint.

fields.label: Text corpus for fitting
fields.help: Use varied text representative of where you intend to read the model. This is not positive/negative concept data. Supply UTF-8 JSONL with one unique id and text per row. Choose existing text, or ask for an authoring prompt; no data is generated automatically.
fields.example: {"id":"sample-1","text":"Replace this sentence with a sufficiently long passage from your chosen, documented corpus."}

fields.label: Corpus preparation receipt
fields.help: Optional preparation.json saved beside a prepared corpus. It records source revisions, selected records, sampling, and token review, and travels with the fitting inputs. Existing manually authored corpora do not need a receipt.

fields.label: Maximum corpus rows (start with a small pilot)
fields.help: Fits the first N rows in file order. Four rows provide a timing pilot, not a well-established lens. Increase after reviewing time, memory, and corpus coverage. Short rows are counted in this limit and recorded as skipped. The request review shows matrix memory and backward-pass estimates when the pinned model configuration is cached locally; otherwise it explains how to obtain an engine estimate.

fields.label: Source layers
fields.help: Blank fits all layers before the final block. Select fewer layers for a cheaper or targeted instrument; token-vector creation needs full coverage. Layer numbers start at zero.

fields.label: Maximum tokens per passage
fields.help: Longer text is truncated to this many tokens. Raw text uses the tokenizer’s native special tokens; no chat template is added.

fields.label: Leading token positions to omit
fields.help: The reference estimator omits early positions and the final token. A passage must have more than this value plus one token after tokenization.

fields.label: Jacobian dimensions per backward pass
fields.help: A memory/performance control. The model repeats the passage this many times per pass. Larger values need more activation memory; start with 1 on a large model. For example, width 5,376 needs 5,376 backward passes per row at batch 1, or 672 at batch 8. Batching uses more activation memory; it does not promise proportional acceleration.

fields.label: Checkpoint every N considered rows
fields.help: A checkpoint may contain several gigabytes. Smaller intervals preserve more progress but increase disk traffic. Active scratch keeps the latest complete snapshot; completed runs retain their final snapshot.

fields.label: Model precision
fields.help: Choose bfloat16, float32, or float16. The fitted Jacobian accumulates and saves in float32. Quantized fitting is not implemented.

fields.label: Python execution device
fields.help: cuda (or cuda:0) on the cluster, mps on a compatible Mac, or cpu for small numerical tests. The pilot must verify backward support on this architecture.

fields.label: Intended lens use
fields.help: testing for rehearsal, or evidence for intended study use. This declaration does not qualify the lens or validate a behavioral interpretation.

fields.label: Continue from a completed checkpoint (optional)
fields.help: Choose state.json beside sums.safetensors after the original job has stopped. Both files travel with the request and are read and verified again at execution; multi-gigabyte files can take several minutes. Continuation creates a new run. Numerical settings and dependency versions must match; documentation-only driver changes do not prevent continuation under the same fitting contract.

fields.label: Compile model blocks
fields.help: Optional speed experiment. Compare gradients and fitted lenses against the uncompiled baseline before using it for a longer run; first-call compilation counts in pilot time.

fields.label: Attention kernel selection
fields.help: current uses this prepared environment; torch explicitly selects inspectable Torch fallback functions. No packages are installed. Compare the two in a small benchmark before changing a continuation runtime.

fields.label: Optional stopping rule document
fields.help: JSON with threshold, window, and minPrompts. Stops after N consecutive available fitted-row changes below the threshold, after the minimum. Leave blank for a fixed row cap; sharded rounds remain fixed-budget.

fields.label: Advanced: explicit global row indices
fields.help: Usually generated by the round planner. Rows remain tied to the original corpus, allowing overlap checks at merge.

fields.label: Optional measured pilot report
fields.help: Choose benchmark-report.json from a matching model, corpus, and fitting configuration to display measured rows per hour and a cautious time extrapolation. This is not a walltime guarantee.

interview.claimBoundary: An averaged Jacobian is an instrument fitted to this corpus and runtime. Stable fitting statistics are not evidence of semantic validity or causal steering effects.
questions: What text population should the lens represent?
How will you assess readouts on held-out text after fitting?
